page: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-96xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server featuring dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. The system provides 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs using x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. This server does not include local storage or GPUs, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier (top 10%) for multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics. Memory bandwidth is also in the top tier for both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads, as well as large-block writes. In database operations, the server achieves top-tier results with high Passmark database scores and 531.59 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. However, while prompt processing for medium and large LLM models ranks in the top tier and strong categories respectively, text generation speeds for small models fall into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture offers direct hardware access and high resource density, eliminating hypervisor overhead. The lack of bundled local storage requires external storage provisioning, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. Given its massive DDR5 memory capacity and top-tier multi-core and database benchmark performance, this server is designed for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy multi-threaded enterprise applications, and high-throughput web serving.
